production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database). First: KBB's 2019 Aventador lists "SVJ Coupe 2D" and says "There's a new ultra-performance Aventador SVJ model for 2019". Last: KBB's 2021 Aventador lists "SVJ Coupe 2D" (kbb-aventador-2021); its 2022 Aventador lists only "Ultimae Coupe 2D" and "Ultimae Convertible 2D" (kbb-aventador-2022). Lamborghini's release (motor1-aventador-svj-release): "The first customers will take delivery of the new Lamborghini Aventador SVJ at the beginning of 2019"; "Production is limited to 900 units". The SVJ Roadster is sold under its own name and is not part of this record.

body.note: Two-door coupe. The Aventador SVJ Roadster is sold under its own name and is not part of this record.

drivetrain.note: Lamborghini release: four-wheel drive (permanent) with rear-wheel steering (LRS).

transmission.note: Lamborghini release (motor1-aventador-svj-release): "optimized seven-speed Independent Shifting Road (ISR) gearbox". ISR is a single-clutch automated manual, as in the LP 700-4 record. No manual offered.

powerHp.note: Quote (Lamborghini history page): "Max. power: 566 kW (770 CV) at 8,500 rpm". 770 CV x 0.98632 = 759 hp. Lamborghini's English release (motor1-aventador-svj-release) prints the metric figure as hp: "the SVJ features an increase in power to 770 hp (566 kW) at maximum 8,500 rpm". Evo panel (evo-aventador-svj): "Power | 759bhp"; KBB: "759 horsepower". No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS, as in the LP 700-4 record.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (guide step 4). Quote (Lamborghini release of 23 August 2018 as reproduced by Motor1): "The SVJ weight just 3,362 pounds (1,525 kilograms) dry". 1,525 x 2.20462 = 3,362 lb. Evo spec panel (evo-aventador-svj): "Weight | 1525kg (dry)". No curb weight for the standard car (steps 1 and 2) and no optioned-car curb weight (step 3) was found from Lamborghini or a major magazine. No opened page says whether the dry figure assumes options. A car with fluids is heavier.
